name: Tiroler Bienenwelt Schönwies
kurzbeschreibung: Tiroler Bienenwelt in Schönwies: an interactive 1,000 m² beekeeping museum with observation beehives, honey tastings, and a show distillery.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Tiroler Bienenwelt is situated in the sunny Oberinntal village of Schönwies in the Tyrolean district of Landeck, at an altitude of approximately 740 metres. Nestled in idyllic scenery between the rugged slopes of the Lechtaler and Ötztaler Alpen, this specialist museum is the largest show and educational centre for beekeeping and apiculture in all of western Austria. Spread over more than 1,000 square metres of contemporary exhibition space, this popular excursion destination is dedicated to the fascinating world of the honeybee, the vital ecological role of pollinating insects in alpine ecosystems, and centuries of Tyrolean beekeeping tradition.

Beekeeping Museum & Observation Hives

Tiroler Bienenwelt was founded by passionate migratory beekeepers eager to share their wealth of knowledge with visitors of all ages. The centerpiece of the museum consists of several living observation hives enclosed in safety glass: here, guests can witness the bustling colony life up close, spot the queen bee laying eggs, and observe the fascinating waggle-dance communication used to signal food sources. Numerous interactive exhibits, tactile touch boxes, scent stations, and glass showcases explain the life cycle of bees and the production of blossom honey, forest honeydew honey, propolis, and royal jelly. A historical department displays rare antique beehives, old centrifugal honey extractors, and tools used by mountain beekeepers over three centuries. The exhibition is complemented by a demonstration distillery crafting honey into fine bee brandy and mead, as well as the popular outdoor Bienen-Lehrpfad (bee nature trail) lined with insect-friendly alpine wildflower meadows.

Visit & Getting There

Tiroler Bienenwelt is open from May to late October from Wednesday to Sunday between 10:00 and 17:00 (closed Mondays and Tuesdays; open in winter on selected days for groups by advance reservation). Admission fees (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €7.00, seniors approx. €6.00, children and youth (ages 6 to 15) approx. €3.50, young children under 6 free; family ticket approx. €16.00. Admission includes a tasting of various Tyrolean mountain honeys. The farm shop in the entrance area can be visited freely without a ticket. Arriving by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Imst or Zams), then follow the B171 to Schönwies (large free car park directly at the museum grounds, Schönwies 34). By public transport: take the ÖBB train (Arlbergbahn railway) to Schönwies station, followed by an easy seven-minute walk through the village to the Bienenwelt.

Tips

The entire exhibition building is completely level and step-free for wheelchair users and pushchairs; the observation hives are installed at child-friendly viewing heights. Sample rare Tyrolean alpine rose honey and forest honey at the tasting bar. In the bee shop, organic natural cosmetics, beeswax candles, and propolis tinctures can be purchased directly from regional beekeepers.
